nativeFacts.fact: Mixed Put old8193->4095, Update old4097->100, Delete8193 and ConditionCheck4097 initially returned 56 WriteCapacityUnits. Immediate replay, replay after scalar overwrites of all four items to16385 bytes, and replay after scalar removal each returned 20 ReadCapacityUnits. Final strong reads found all four absent: replays did not restore items or reevaluate the now-failing ConditionCheck.

Each individual Put/Update/Delete/ConditionCheck at4096/4097 bytes returned initial8/10 WriteCapacityUnits and replay2/4 ReadCapacityUnits. Update shrank the original item to100 bytes, Delete removed it, and ConditionCheck made no data change. Replay charges remained identical after external growth to16385 bytes and removal. Together with the mixed old-larger Put case, observations support retained original max(before,after) item-size read charges, not current-image or post-write-only charges; this is a sampled inference, not a general index/attribute-size formula. Native ConditionCheck initial capacity is reported in WriteCapacityUnits, including Table, not ReadCapacityUnits.

ExecuteTransaction INSERT of4097 bytes returned10 WriteCapacityUnits; immediate replay and replay after scalar growth to16385 bytes and removal each returned4 ReadCapacityUnits. Strong reads confirmed the external grown item was preserved and the removed item stayed absent.

Reversing JSON map member order at every nesting level was equivalent. Numeric AttributeValues1,1.0,1e0,01,+1 were equivalent in both APIs. Omitted and explicitNONE were equivalent for ReturnConsumedCapacity, ReturnItemCollectionMetrics (classic only), and ReturnValuesOnConditionCheckFailure. A trailing space in the PartiQL statement was equivalent. This samples structural/semantic equality; it does not establish all numeric, set, expression, or statement canonicalization.

Changing ReturnConsumedCapacityINDEXES toTOTAL/NONE, addingINDEXES after omitted capacity, changing collection metrics toSIZE, or reversing transaction item/statement array order produced IdempotentParameterMismatchException. Original payloads still replayed successfully after rejected variants. No error response included ConsumedCapacity; omitted capacity is unknown, not zero.

Reusing a token for a different table produced mismatch in both APIs, so tokens are not independently namespaced per table. A successful classic request blocked a different ExecuteTransaction payload with the same token, and a successful ExecuteTransaction blocked a different classic payload; both original requests still replayed. The APIs share token identity namespace within the tested account/region. No other account, region or principal scope was exercised.

Conditional classic cancellation and PartiQL duplicate-item cancellation retained token payload identity: changed payloads mismatched. Identical original requests succeeded after external state repair and subsequent replay returned read rather than write capacity. Thus canceled results were not permanently replayed, but cancellation did not release the token for arbitrary changed requests. Cancellation errors omitted capacity.

A syntactically invalid classic UpdateExpression and malformed PartiQL statement returned ValidationException. A corrected, different payload reused each token successfully with2 WriteCapacityUnits, then identical replay returned2 ReadCapacityUnits. These front-end syntax failures did not reserve identity; other validation stages/errors remain unmeasured.

The initial probe stopped after incorrectly requiring changed-payload reuse after cancellation to succeed; that native mismatch and all original calls remain intact. Both tables were deleted and verified absent. The same owned table-a name was recreated to complete failure cases with fresh tokens, then deleted and verified ResourceNotFoundException at196; table-b was verified absent at163. Only these two table names were used. No ten-minute expiry wait was performed.

experiment.sizeRule: ASCII string attribute names and values summed; excludes storage overhead.
experiment.retentionMatrix: Individual Put/Update/Delete/ConditionCheck at 4096 and 4097 bytes; immediate replay, scalar overwrite with 16385 bytes, replay, scalar removal, replay. Update shrinks to 100 bytes. Mixed transaction has distinct before/after sizes.

limitations: CLI input JSON and modeled native output/errors, not raw HTTP bytes. Map insertion order is preserved in recorded inputs.
No capacity is assumed on errors or when ConsumedCapacity is omitted; CloudWatch failure-path consumption is not measured.
Ten-minute expiry is documented, not wall-clock tested. All comparisons must be interpreted with their recorded timestamps.
Only the approved account and region were tested; no cross-account, cross-region, index, in-flight, or expiry scope inference.
Equivalent numeric strings and map order are sampled; this is not an exhaustive semantic canonicalization specification.

continuation.reason: Initial script incorrectly required changed-payload reuse after cancellation to succeed; native mismatch preserved. Recreated the same owned table name after verified deletion to complete failure-path matrix with fresh tokens.
